passage: I'm Samir. Kunal used to grumble that his father made him be home by nine, even when everyone else's curfews were later. Last night we were at my cousin's wedding and it ran late. Kunal's phone lit up. "Dad is outside," he said. "He has been sitting in the car for two hours because I said I might be late." He wasn't grumbling. He said, "I used to hate that rule. I think it was just him worrying." I can't know what he felt, but he was quiet all the way to the gate, and he thanked his father twice before he even got in the car.

qa.q: How long had Kunal's father been sitting in the car?
qa.a: He had been sitting in the car for two hours.

qa.q: What did Kunal seem to realise about his father's rule?
qa.a: He seemed to realise that the rule came from worry and care, not from wanting to control him.

qa.q: How could Kunal tell his father what he has understood?
qa.a: He could thank him plainly and, when the time is right, ask to talk about the hour as he grows older. 🙂

qa.q: How might Kunal's father see the nine o'clock rule?
qa.a: He probably made it out of worry, and waiting in the car for two hours suggests it was about care for Kunal.

grounding: An observer sees a teen realise that a parent's limit was care.
